goodrich.title: Data Structures and Algorithms in Python
goodrich.authors: Michael T. Goodrich, Roberto Tamassia and Michael H. Goldwasser

data-structure-concepts-and-arrays.read: Chapters 1 and 4: Introduction and Overview; Arrays, Records and Pointers
data-structure-concepts-and-arrays.why: Classifies data structures and gives the array addressing formulas the past papers use.

linked-lists.why: Singly, doubly and circular lists with insertion, deletion and traversal.

stacks-and-expressions.why: Stack operations and infix, prefix and postfix conversion and evaluation.

queues-and-deques.why: Queues, circular queues, deques and priority queues.

trees-and-search-trees.why: Binary trees, traversal, expression trees, binary search trees, AVL trees and B-trees.
Python versions of traversal, BSTs, AVL and red-black trees, matching the papers' Python questions.

graphs.why: Adjacency matrices and lists, DFS, BFS and spanning trees.

sorting-searching-and-hashing.why: Sorting and searching algorithms, hashing and collision resolution.
